items.title: Shelf Life 123: Nostalgia As a Band-Aid
items.summary_original: Gen Z nostalgia has become branding’s safest creative shortcut, but when every rebrand looks backward, nostalgia stops feeling strategic and starts feeling stale. Designers and strategists weigh in on why brands keep mining the past, the risks of breaking with familiarity, and what truly forward-thinking brand design could look like. The post Shelf Life 123: Nostalgia As a Band-Aid appeared first on DIELINE .
items.title_de: Haltbarkeit 123: Nostalgie als Pflaster

Designer und Strategen äußern sich zu den Gründen, warum Marken weiterhin in der Vergangenheit schwelgen, zu welchen Risiken ein Bruch mit Vertrautem führt und wie ein wirklich zukunftsorientiertes Markendesign aussehen könnte. Der Beitrag „Shelf Life 123: Nostalgie als Pflaster“ erschien zuerst auf DIELINE.

items.summary_original: Upcycled Computer Hardware Forms a DIY CD Player CD-ROM PLAYER 01 by das_POD is a DIY audio project that repurposes used computer CD-ROM drives as the basis for a functional CD player . items.summary_original: ASTON MARTIN VALEN PREVIEW BEFORE MONTEREY CAR WEEK 2026 During a preview at the British marque's headquarters in Gaydon, UK, designboom examines the Aston Martin Valen prior to its public debut at The Quail during Monterey Car Week 2026 . Members of the manufacturer's Special Vehicle Operations (SVO) team presented the front-engined supercar , explaining how it serves as an experimental alter ego alongside other bespoke low-volume projects such as the Valour , Valiant , and DBR22. Constructed with a full carbon fiber body and engineered with custom 3D printing, the supercar demonstrates how Aston Martin's bespoke division extends past external coachwork into technical novelties under the bonnet. the profile of the Aston Martin Valen highlights its low cabin, wide track, and broken S-curve
items.title_de: Vorschau: Die Kohlefaserkarosserie des limitierten Aston Martin Valen ist mit Interferenzlackierung überzogen

Mitglieder des Special Vehicle Operations (SVO)-Teams des Herstellers stellten den Supersportwagen mit Frontmotor vor und erklärten, wie er neben anderen maßgeschneiderten Kleinserienprojekten wie Valor, Valiant und DBR22 als experimentelles Alter Ego dient. The project retains traces of the building's accumulated history while introducing new elements through a material and formal language that connects the existing structure with its garden setting. For generations, the property was associated with the family's timber business. items.title: Unsichtbares sichtbar machen: Serviceplan redesignt Ultra Rare Sarcoma e.V.
items.summary_original: Wie man eine Krankheit unübersehbar macht, über die kaum jemand spricht, zeigt Serviceplan in seiner neuen, eindrucksvollen Markenidentität der Ultra Rare Sarcoma e.V. Die Ultra Rare Sarcoma e.V. ist ein gemeinnütziger Patientenverein in München, der eine Anlaufstelle für Menschen mit sehr seltenen Sarkomen ist. Die bösartigen Tumore entstehen im Binde-, Stütz- oder Muskelgewebe und gehören zu den am wenigsten erforschten Krebsarten weltweit. Der Verein möchte das ändern, die Krankheit sichtbar machen und Betroffene unterstützen. Und das mit einem Team von Fachleuten, von Ärzten und Patienten, die sich für »mehr Wissen, bessere Therapien und echte Perspektiven« einsetzen, für die Finanzierung von Forschung und die Vernetzung von Betroffenen und Angehörigen. Was für eine essenzielle Arbeit

items.summary_original: a potter’s wedging stand transforms into a cat-shaped bench Designed by MACH Architects Beijing for ceramic artists, this bench reimagines the traditional potter’s wedging stand as a compact piece of furniture that combines ergonomic considerations with familiar woodworking techniques. These stands typically feature a forward-leaning slope to ease clay wedging, a silhouette strikingly similar to a stretching cat . The design releases the cat hidden within this functional form. the bench reinterprets the traditional potter’s wedging stand | all images ©MACH Architects Beijing Timber structure and playful mechanisms refine the bench’s form Starting with a conventional bench, the designers at MACH Architects Beijing narrowed the width and calibrated the incline to optimise ergonomic comfort.

Texts in both German and English offer access to the diverse perspectives, approaches, and ideas developed by the graduates. The magazine opens with a visual table of contents that functions not only as an orientation tool but also as a creative introduction to the publication and its wide range of projects. items.summary_original: Folded Steel Defines the Asymmetrical Form of TABLE LAMP Z Designed by Cobre Estudio, TABLE LAMP Z explores how a simple manufacturing process can generate a distinctive and expressive lighting object. The project starts from a single sheet of 2 mm steel , using laser cutting and folding as the main processes to define both its structure and its visual identity. The lamp is conceived around the exploration of folded sheet-metal surfaces and the relationship between geometry, balance, and visual weight. Its asymmetrical configuration creates an intentional sense of imbalance, while the precise folds provide the structural stability required for everyday use. Das Projekt beginnt mit einem einzelnen 2-mm-Stahlblech, dessen Hauptprozesse Laserschneiden und Falten sind, um sowohl seine Struktur als auch seine visuelle Identität zu definieren. Seine asymmetrische Konfiguration erzeugt bewusst ein Gefühl der Unausgewogenheit, während die präzisen Falten für die für den täglichen Gebrauch erforderliche strukturelle Stabilität sorgen. items.title: What Star Wars got wrong about AI (so far)
items.summary_original: Two generations learned what a thinking machine looks like from a production line of individuals and the picture is not holding. AI assisted. The saga imagined thinking machines as immortal individuals in metal bodies. Real AI showed up as copyable software, and every difference is worth understanding. We grew up with the droids. R2-D2 beeping through a firefight, C-3PO fretting about the odds of survival, a whole galaxy quietly run by machines that think. Many of the androids from Star Wars are the most likable robots in film, and they are also the wrong picture of artificial intelligence. That matters more than it should, because for two generations the droids were most people’s first and clearest mental model of a thinking machine and mental models, once they take hold, change is hard.
items.title_de: Was Star Wars in Bezug auf KI falsch gemacht hat (bisher)

items.title: Constrictor
items.summary_original: Constrictor , a new type family released by Frere-Jones Type in June 2026, began as a title sketch for a documentary about Margaret Lovatt, who was part of a NASA funded project which set out to communicate with dolphins and ended up dosing them with LSD. Shallcrass layered this rich input with typographic history, experiences and memories from the physical world to create a variable font family which radiates an energetic presence and has movement at its core. According to Shallcrass, "Danger, tension and anxiety are key aspects of why the face works to me." Constrictor's variable width axis impacts our perception of noise when read: expand the letters and you can feel the rhythm ease; compress them and the letterforms begin to grip each other like a boa constrictor finding its hold. items.title: What a dollhouse full of death taught me about thinking
items.summary_original: How models change what we notice, question, and understand Tiny furniture [Content warning: This article contains images of miniature death scenes.] I recently started building a miniature house in my free time. However, not every dollhouse is built to make you feel safe or comforted. One example is Frances Glessner Lee’s collection of miniature death scenes. We were designing the onboarding for an AI product, the first time user experience that tries to prove the product is worth their time. The fairly insignificant thing we were fighting about was whether to add a little animation that made it look like the software was thinking hard, adding a few seconds to the flow when really it could have been instantaneous. items.title_de: Wir verschlingen uns mit geliehenem Vertrauen und das wird uns teuer zu stehen kommen.
items.summary_de: Das vertrauenswürdige Gesicht ist die Maske, aber die Maschine darunter weiß nicht, wann es falsch ist, und genau das werden Sie nicht überprüfen. Je mehr wir einem Namen vertrauen, desto weniger stellen wir die Maschine in Frage, die ihn trägt, und desto mehr muss dieser Name verlieren, wenn die Maschine selbstbewusst falsch liegt. Vor ein paar Wochen hat mein Team eine Stunde lang darüber gestritten, ob man die Leute anlügen soll. Wir haben das Onboarding für ein KI-Produkt entworfen, das erste Benutzererlebnis, das beweisen soll, dass das Produkt seine Zeit wert ist. Die ziemlich unbedeutende Sache, über die wir gestritten haben, war, ob wir eine kleine Animation hinzufügen sollten, die den Anschein erweckte, als würde die Software angestrengt nachdenken, und so den Ablauf um ein paar Sekunden verlängern, obwohl er eigentlich augenblicklich hätte erfolgen können. Ein rasanter „Analysiere deine Antworten…“-Moment, in dem wir etwas Sprache und BH einbringen konnten

items.summary_original: a sky full of hope moves above frankfurt Janet Echelman has spent much of her career persuading cities to look up. Her newest public artwork hangs over Konstablerwache, a broad central square in Frankfurt where commuters pass through and a market takes over twice a week. A Sky Full of Hope – Earthtime 1.78 Frankfurt stretches a field of colored fiber more than seven meters overhead, moving with the wind through the day and illumination after dark. More than 3,000 people gathered beneath it for its August 11th unveiling, filling the square and occupying nearly every deck chair by the afternoon. For the 9th Triennial of Photography Hamburg 2026, dipshop developed a visual identity based on three phenomena that are usually present in photographs but rarely become the subject themselves: depth of field, lens flares and burned film. Rather than treating them as technical side effects, we turned them into the building blocks of the festival’s graphic language. The resulting identity shifts attention away from photographic representation and towards the medium’s overlooked elements—those that shape how we see images, yet often remain invisible. items.summary_original: SHIJI COMMONS transforms two stone houses into community hub Located in Hengshiji Village, Sanzao Town, Zhuhai, China , SHIJI COMMONS by StudioTiltedCircle transforms two traditional stone houses into a contemporary community space. Situated between the village fabric and the surrounding landscape, the project explores how an existing rural structure can be renewed while preserving its material memory and cultural identity. Rather than replacing the old, the project begins with the existing stone walls. Through dismantling, reclaiming, and reusing the original stone, the material is transformed from a structural element into a new spatial interface. SHIJI COMMONS von StudioTiltedCircle befindet sich im Dorf Hengshiji, Stadt Sanzao, Zhuhai, China und verwandelt zwei traditionelle Steinhäuser in einen modernen Gemeinschaftsraum. items.summary_original: a pair of towers between the mountains and the adriatic Along Albania ’s southern coast, OODA has designed DUAS Towers as a pair of 98-meter mixed-use buildings rising above Vlorë, a city which sits between the mountains and the Adriatic Sea. One tower is circular and the other quadrangular, yet both follow the same architectural system. A horizontal volume forms the base, an upright slab rises through the center, and another horizontal piece closes the composition overhead. Their name follows the pairing too. Duas is Portuguese for two. The difference between the two appears most clearly from a distance. The rectangular tower measures 30 by 25 meters, while its neighbor forms a 26-meter-wide circle. Ein Turm ist kreisförmig und der andere viereckig, doch beide folgen demselben architektonischen System. Ein horizontales Volumen bildet die Basis, eine aufrechte Platte erhebt sich durch die Mitte und ein weiteres horizontales Stück schließt die Komposition über dem Kopf ab. items.title: Is there a retirement crisis in the creative industry?
items.summary_original: Retirement plans are changing for creatives. Image licensed via Adobe Stock Right now, senior creatives are planning to exit the industry much earlier than expected. So what exactly is going on? There's a conversation in creative industries right now that's largely going under the radar. items.title_de: Gibt es in der Kreativbranche eine Ruhestandskrise?
items.summary_de: Die Ruhestandspläne für Kreative ändern sich. Bild lizenziert über Adobe Stock Derzeit planen erfahrene Kreative, die Branche viel früher als erwartet zu verlassen. Was genau ist also los? In der Kreativbranche gibt es derzeit eine Diskussion, die weitgehend unter dem Radar bleibt. Es passiert in Direktnachrichten, in geflüsterten Gesprächen bei Branchenveranstaltungen und um 3 Uhr morgens, wenn die Leute nicht schlafen können. Das Gespräch beginnt damit: „Ich glaube, ich muss in den Ruhestand gehen.“ Nehmen Sie den Illustrator und Designer Jason Roberts. „Ich bin innerhalb kürzester Zeit von dem Gedanken ‚Ich werde vielleicht nie in Rente gehen‘ zu ‚Ich muss vielleicht früher in Rente gehen‘ übergegangen“, gibt er zu. „Ich dachte wirklich, dass ich nie genug verdienen würde, um wirklich in Rente zu gehen. Aber wenn KI mich aus meiner eigenen Branche verdrängen würde, müsste ich vielleicht früher in den Ruhestand gehen, einen Weg finden, über die Runden zu kommen, oder vielleicht meine Arbeit verkaufen.“
